div.p: The traditional mental health management model often relies on students to actively seek help, which has certain limitations. With the development of big data and artificial intelligence technology, sentiment analysis methods based on students' social texts provide new ideas for campus mental health monitoring. This study developed a college student mental health monitoring system based on social text sentiment analysis. The system uses sentiment dictionaries and LSTM, a text classification model based on deep learning, to perform real-time sentiment analysis on texts, pictures, videos and other content posted by students on campus social platforms, thereby identifying abnormal signals such as negative emotions and anxiety. The experimental test results show that the LSTM model is superior to the basic RNN model in key indicators such as sentiment analysis accuracy and response time, and can better meet the requirements of the mental health monitoring system for real-time and accuracy. In summary, this study shows that the social text sentiment analysis technology can effectively improve the monitoring ability of campus mental health management and provide an important basis for early intervention.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the continuous development of higher education, the mental health of college students has attracted widespread attention from all walks of life. Relevant surveys show that more than 30% of college students in China face psychological problems such as anxiety and depression, and the risk of suicidal behavior cannot be ignored. As an important position for cultivating future pillars of society, colleges and universities must attach great importance to the management and service of students' mental health.

The traditional mental health management model often relies on students to actively seek help, which has certain limitations. Many students may be unwilling or unable to seek help for various reasons when facing psychological distress, which leads to the aggravation of the problem. With the rapid development of big data and artificial intelligence technology, sentiment analysis based on a large amount of text content posted by students on campus social platforms provides new possibilities for colleges and universities to establish intelligent mental health monitoring systems. By capturing the subtle signals of students' emotional changes in real time, timely discovering abnormal situations and combining them with the school's mental health indicator system, it can help school administrators take targeted intervention measures in time to maintain students' mental health. This paper first introduces the overall architecture of the mental health monitoring system based on social text sentiment analysis, and explains the correlation between sentiment analysis results and mental health indicators. Subsequently, the data set used in the system experimental test is detailed, and the system performance based on two different model structures, LSTM and RNN, is compared and analyzed. Finally, this paper comprehensively evaluates the overall performance of the system from multiple dimensions and looks forward to future development trends.

div.head: II. RELATED WORK
div.p: There have been many studies on issues related to mental health monitoring. Wang Chao designed a monitoring model for the mental health of employees in tobacco companies, inputting psychological state indicators into the model to monitor the mental health status of company employees. The test results showed that the monitoring results of the system were basically consistent with the actual results, and the monitoring accuracy was high, which had great feasibility [1]. Liu Yue achieved comprehensive management and attention to students' mental health by establishing a lifelong electronic psychological record. At the same time, through a student mental health dynamic detection system based on big data, combined with feedback information from multiple dimensions such as "home school" and "teacher student", the psychological status of students can be monitored throughout the entire cycle, thereby achieving timely intervention and treatment of students' psychological problems [2]. Li Yaling divided the system design into three parts using B/S structure: client, application, and database. After logging into the system, the client user analyzes the user's personality through personality feature dimension assignment and weight calculation in the personality feature module, and tests the user's mental health status through multiple scales in the personality testing module. The user's personality features and test results are converted into digital form and uploaded to the network [3]. Yang Wenxin developed a system to address the mental health issues of college students, which plays an important role in their mental health [4]. In order to improve the mental health level and work efficiency of prison police, Liu Weiyi used a survey questionnaire to evaluate the mental health status and occupational burnout level of in-service police officers in a prison in Hunan Province. The research results showed that factors such as education level, social support, and coping strategies were significantly correlated with mental health [5]. Ahmed T comprehensively evaluated the latest technologies for measuring cortisol and Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and their applications in human stress monitoring [6]. Chakraborty A aimed to address the issue of preventing mental health disorders by using the developed portal website "Mind Turner" for early prediction of individuals [7]. Ji X proposed a highly efficient memristive sequence network (EMSN) for human emotion classification, which provides consumers with a low-cost, easy to deploy, and environmentally friendly method [8]. Arrow K evaluated the feasibility and effectiveness of using online self-report questionnaires to supplement clinical assessments of individuals with or without a diagnosis of mental illness [9]. Vriend E described the anxiety and depression symptoms and risk factors of parents at 1 month and 12 months of age correction [10]. Existing research relies on actively seeking help, which has certain limitations. This article will construct a university student mental health monitoring system based on social text sentiment analysis to address these issues.

div.head: A. Campus Social Platforms
div.p: In the psychological health monitoring system based on social text sentiment analysis, it is crucial to fully utilize campus social platforms as data sources. Campus social platforms, as the main channel for daily communication among college students, can provide rich textual data that reflects students' emotional states, life dynamics, and psychological changes. Campus social platforms usually have a wide coverage, and most students engage in daily communication on the platform. The content is rich, including various aspects such as learning, life, and emotions, and is updated frequently, which can capture real-time changes in students' emotions [11]. Therefore, data collection based on campus social platforms can better reflect the overall mental health status of college students. In terms of data collection, it is first necessary to obtain authorization and permission from the school or platform management to ensure that the data collection behavior is legal and compliant. Then, web crawling technology can be used to regularly capture text data posted by students on social media platforms, including text, images, videos, and other multimedia content. In order to protect student privacy, the collected data can be anonymized, such as anonymizing user IDs, while establishing a sound data storage and management mechanism to ensure data security. div.head: B. Construction of Emotional Dictionary
div.p: Building an emotional dictionary for campus students to better support a social text-based mental health monitoring system. Firstly, the school invited experts from the psychological counseling center and student representatives to form a dictionary construction team. The group members first collected a large number of commonly used words in students' daily communication, covering multiple aspects such as learning, life, and interpersonal communication. Through preliminary screening, they ultimately determined an initial vocabulary list containing 500 words. Next, the group members will rate the emotional polarity of these 500 words. The emotional tendency of each word is independently scored by three experts and three student representatives, with a scoring range of [-1,1]. For example, the word "effort" is classified as a positive emotion if three experts rate it as 0.8, 0.9, or 0.7, and three students rate it as 0.7, 0.8, or 0.9, with an average value of 0.8. The term 'anxiety' is rated as negative emotion by three experts with scores of -0.7, -0.6, and -0.8, and three students with scores of -0.6, -0.7, and -0.7, with an average of -0.68 [12]. After multiple rounds of evaluation and discussion, the group ultimately determined the sentiment scores and categories for 500 words. In order to further improve the accuracy of sentiment analysis, the team also developed semantic based dynamic sentiment evaluation rules for some context sensitive words. For example, the word 'disappointment' may express negative emotions in a learning context, but may express neutral or positive emotions in daily life [13]. div.head: C. Emotion Analysis Model Based on Machine Learning
div.p: For this type of short text data, deep learning-based text classification algorithms are particularly effective at capturing the emotional features hidden within the text. Among these algorithms, LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) and Transformer models have gained widespread attention due to their distinct advantages in processing sequential data. LSTM networks excel at learning contextual information over time, allowing them to understand the relationships between words in a sequence and maintain memory of previous inputs. Similarly, the attention mechanism is employed by the transformer models to model the associations of words and also allows the model the ability to weigh the words against each other. With both processes demonstrating high levels of sentiment analysis capability, these techniques are wellpositioned to examine the subtle emotional states of college students as they express their feelings on social media. [14].

In the model construction process, the first step involves extracting emotional features from the text based on a carefully constructed college student sentiment dictionary. This dictionary serves as a reference for identifying and categorizing emotions expressed in the text. Text data can be numerically represented using methods such as Word Frequency Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), which transforms textual information into vectors that reflect the importance of each word in relation to the entire dataset. Once these feature vectors are generated, they are fed into either LSTM or Transformer models for training. This training phase focuses on learning the emotional expression patterns present in the text. The primary objective is to minimize the error between the actual emotional labels and the predicted emotions as determined by the model. By iteratively refining the model's predictions, it can better understand and classify the emotional content of student texts, ultimately leading to more accurate assessments of their psychological well-being. This process not only enhances sentiment analysis capabilities but also supports the development of more effective mental health monitoring systems for college students. that is shown in eq. ( 2).

div.head: D. Correlation Between Sentiment Analysis Results and Mental Health Indicators
div.p: Universities will apply the constructed sentiment dictionary and deep learning-based text sentiment analysis model to analyze students' social platform data effectively. By continuously monitoring various types of content, including text, images, videos, and other multimedia posted by students on campus social networks, the system can capture subtle signals of emotional changes in real time. This proactive approach allows for timely interventions and support, as emotional fluctuations can often indicate underlying mental health issues. For instance, consider a specific student who, during a certain period, frequently posted negative emotional words on social media, such as "too tired," "lack of motivation," and "feeling lonely." The sentiment analysis model, utilizing the sentiment dictionary and deep learning techniques, accurately classified these texts as reflecting negative emotions. This classification is crucial, as it provides valuable insights into the student's emotional state and overall well-being. Upon further analysis based on the student's mental health indicators, we discovered that his learning anxiety index is significantly high, indicating that he experiences considerable stress and pressure related to his academic performance. Additionally, his interpersonal communication index is notably low, suggesting difficulties in social interactions and connections with peers. This isolation may contribute to his feelings of loneliness and lack of motivation. Furthermore, the student's life satisfaction is also reported to be poor, which could have detrimental effects on his overall mental health and academic success.

By integrating sentiment analysis with mental health indicators, universities can create a comprehensive monitoring system that not only identifies students at risk but also provides targeted support. This system enables counselors and mental health professionals to intervene early, offering resources and strategies tailored to each student's unique situation. Ultimately, this approach fosters a healthier campus environment, promoting emotional well-being and academic success among students, while also highlighting the importance of leveraging technology in mental health initiatives within educational institutions [15].

In this case, the mental health monitoring system can automatically identify the existence of certain psychological problems and promptly alert the school's psychological counseling center. The school can then arrange professional psychological counselors to intervene and provide targeted psychological counseling to help students alleviate anxiety, improve interpersonal communication, and enhance life satisfaction. By deeply integrating the results of sentiment analysis with psychological health indicators, the psychological health monitoring system of universities can not only detect abnormal situations in a timely manner, but also provide strong support for the school to formulate accurate psychological health management measures. This not only helps maintain students' mental health, but also injects new impetus into the construction of a harmonious campus environment in schools.

div.head: A. Dataset Introduction
div.p: The dataset used in this experiment comes from the campus social platform of a university, which includes the text content posted by students on the platform. The data collection period spans from January 2022 to June 2023, covering a complete academic year. During the data collection process, student privacy information has been anonymized to ensure data compliance. A total of 150000 student social text data were collected, covering various aspects such as learning, life, and interpersonal communication. The average length of each text data is 120 characters. The collected social text data is manually annotated by psychological counseling experts and trained student assistants, with annotation dimensions including emotional polarity (positive, negative, neutral) and emotional categories (such as anxiety, depression, excitement, etc.). The annotation process undergoes multiple discussions and corrections to ensure the accuracy and consistency of the annotation results.

div.head: C. Performance Testing of Mental Health Monitoring
div.p: System When testing the system constructed in this article, the Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) algorithm was selected as the control algorithm for testing, and the coverage rate and response time of mental health monitoring were selected as indicators for evaluation. Among them, 12 classes were selected for the coverage test, and the response time was tested through multiple repeated experiments. Figure 3 shows the coverage test results, and Figure 4 shows the response time test results: From the test results, it is evident that the LSTM-based mental health monitoring system significantly outperforms the RNN-based system in terms of mental health monitoring coverage. The coverage of the LSTM model fluctuates between 96.5% and 98.8%, with an impressive average of 97.6%. In contrast, the coverage of the RNN model is relatively low, ranging from 94.5% to 95.8%, with an average of only 95.1%. This disparity highlights the effectiveness of the LSTM architecture in capturing the nuances of emotional expression over time. Furthermore, the LSTM-based mental health monitoring system excels in response time as well. The average response time of the LSTM model is 0.16 seconds, with the fastest recorded response reaching a remarkable 0.08 seconds. In comparison, the RNN model has an average response time of 0.25 seconds, with the fastest response being only 0.18 seconds. This difference can be attributed to the fact that LSTM is a specialized type of recurrent neural network (RNN) designed to better capture long-range dependencies in text sequences. This capability enables LSTM to more effectively understand the emotional states of students, allowing it to process context more thoroughly than basic RNNs. As a result, the superior performance of the LSTM model in both coverage and response time provides a stronger advantage in social text sentiment analysis tasks. This enhanced capability not only improves the accuracy of mental health assessments but also facilitates timely interventions, ultimately contributing to better support for students experiencing emotional challenges. By leveraging the strengths of LSTM, educational institutions can create more effective mental health monitoring systems that are responsive to the needs of their students, fostering a healthier academic environment.

div.head: V. CONCLUSION
div.p: The system designed in this article applies sentiment lexicon and deep learning based text classification model LSTM to perform real-time sentiment analysis on students' social texts, identifying abnormal signals such as negative emotions and anxiety states. Then, these sentiment analysis results are correlated with the school's pre-defined mental health indicators to construct a comprehensive mental health profile of students. Once a student is found to have abnormal emotions or psychological problems, the system can issue timely warnings, providing strong support for the school's mental health intervention work. The experimental test results show that the LSTM model outperforms the basic RNN model in key indicators such as sentiment analysis accuracy and response time, and can better meet the real-time and accuracy requirements of mental health monitoring systems. In the future, with the further application of big data and artificial intelligence technology in schools, the psychological health monitoring system based on social text will continue to be improved and expanded. It can introduce multimodal sentiment analysis methods, such as combining students' behavioral characteristics in campus videos, images, etc., to construct a more intelligent psychological state assessment model.

figure.figDesc: Fig. 2. Model performance evaluationWith the increase of training sample size, the accuracy and recall of sentiment analysis models have significantly improved. When the training sample size is small, the accuracy and recall are both low, only reaching 46.6% and 39.6%, respectively. But as the scale of training data gradually expands, both indicators show a relatively stable upward trend. When the training sample size reaches 1500, the accuracy and recall rates reach 95.2% and 87.6%, respectively. Further increasing the training set size to 2000 samples, the accuracy and recall rates further improve to 95.8% and 93%, respectively. By continuously expanding high-quality training data and adopting appropriate deep learning model structures, social text-based sentiment analysis systems can achieve significant improvements in accuracy and recall.
